html:
Pegu, now Bago, is a city in Lower Burma that was the capital of the Mon kingdom of Hanthawaddy and later of a great Burmese empire. The map shows it from 1492 to 1600.

After Pagan fell, the Mon set up their own kingdom in 1287, and from 1369 Pegu was its capital. It fought the Burmese kingdom of Ava in the Forty Years' War from 1385 to 1424. Its golden age came under Queen Shin Sawbu, who ruled from 1454 to 1471, and her successor Dhammazedi. Pegu grew rich on sea trade and was a centre of Theravada Buddhism.

The Taungoo king Tabinshwehti conquered it in 1538 and 1539 and made it his capital. His successor Bayinnaung ruled from Pegu the largest empire in Southeast Asian history, taking Ayutthaya in 1564 and again in 1569. In 1599 forces from Arakan (Mrauk U) and Taungoo sacked the city. Its story continues in Taungoo and Konbaung Burma.
